decisions.choice: the LORD sent Nathan: God answers what David did in chapter 11
decisions.reason: The last words of chapter 11 were that what David had done was evil in Yahweh's eyes (11:27). Now Yahweh acts. Nathan is the prophet who brought David the promise of a lasting house (7:2-17); he now brings God's judgment.

decisions.choice: two men: a story told as a case for the king to judge
decisions.reason: Nathan does not say at first that this is a parable. He tells it like a real complaint brought to the king, who was the highest judge in the land (15:2-4). David is meant to give his verdict before he sees that the case is about himself. A wise woman uses the same method in 14:4-11, and a prophet in 1 Kings 20:39-41.

decisions.choice: poor: a man with little or nothing
decisions.reason: The word describes someone without property or means (Proverbs 13:23; 1 Samuel 18:23, where David calls himself "a poor man"). It sets up the contrast with the rich man's many flocks.

decisions.choice: Nathan came to him
decisions.reason: Readable names Nathan, where the Hebrew says only "he", so that the reader does not take the subject to be David.

decisions.choice: Nathan's story in the imperfect and the passé composé at every level ("il y avait", "il a pris")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The parable is speech to the king, told as a case for him to judge (m2), so it takes the tenses of spoken French at every level, as the style guide sets for stories told inside speech. The quotation stays open to the end of verse 4.

decisions.choice: "Natán"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note and the published Psalm 51 title. The parable is drafted from the Hebrew gloss, as the Samuel terms note asks for this chapter.

decisions.choice: Nathan tells the story to "vua" as a case to be judged, without any address in it
decisions.reason: Nathan calls David "vua" as the Samuel terms note sets; the story itself is told plainly, as a case brought before the king (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Nathan tells his story to the king in the formal polite style (합쇼체), as a case brought for judgment
alternatives: the plain narrative style inside the story
decisions.reason: A subject presenting a case to the king speaks 합쇼체 throughout; the story's own events are told with -었습니다.

decisions.choice: Natã
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the prophet is "Natã", the usual Brazilian form, with the nasal ending of "Miriã" and "Midiã", as in chapter 7 and Luke 3:31 in Portuguese.

decisions.choice: one little ewe lamb: a single animal kept as part of the family
decisions.reason: A poor household might own one lamb and raise it by hand. This one is treated like a child of the house: it eats the man's own food and sleeps in his arms. Its loss is the loss of something loved, not only of property.

decisions.choice: would eat, would drink, would lie: what happened day after day
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe the lamb's daily life with the family, not a single meal.

decisions.choice: lay in his bosom ... like a daughter: words that point toward the real case
decisions.reason: "Bosom" is the word for a close embrace, used of a wife in verse 8 and in Deuteronomy 13:7; 28:54. The lamb is "like a daughter" (Hebrew *bat*), and the woman in chapter 11 is Bathsheba, whose name begins with the same word. The story is told so that David can hear it as being about a man's beloved, though he does not yet see it.

decisions.choice: his sons: his children
decisions.reason: The plural of "son" often covers a man's children of both sexes. Nothing in the story limits it to boys.

decisions.choice: shared his bit of bread, lay in his arms (Balanced); ate from his plate, slept in his arms (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Morsel" is a piece of bread, a share of the man's own meal; Readable says "ate from his plate". "Bosom" becomes "arms". Readable adds "even" to show that this is the most striking detail.

decisions.choice: ses {{gender:enfants|fils}}
decisions.reason: The plural covers a man's children of both sexes (m4), so French takes the inclusive "enfants" by default, as the English does; "brebis" and "agnelle" keep the female animal, which the story uses to point toward Bathsheba.

decisions.choice: "sus hijos", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already takes in daughters, so the English gender span on "children" / "sons" has no Spanish counterpart, as the Pentateuch note sets.

decisions.choice: watoto wake
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span on "children|sons". "Watoto" (children) is the natural Swahili word for a man's family at home; the traditional "wana" would not narrow the meaning, so there is no span.

decisions.choice: "các con" with no gender setting
alternatives: "các con trai" as a second wording
decisions.reason: His sons are his children (meaning decision); Vietnamese "các con" includes both, so the English gender setting has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "자식들" (L) and "아이들" (R) with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: The Korean words already mean children of both sexes.

decisions.choice: a cordeirinha
decisions.reason: The diminutive "cordeirinha" says in one word that the lamb was small and female (m1) and carries the tenderness of a pet raised by hand, which is the point of the story; Literal adds "uma só" for "one".

decisions.choice: os seus filhos, without a gender setting
decisions.reason: Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters (m4), as in the Pentateuch and 1 Samuel in Portuguese, so there is no second wording for the English gender setting to choose.

es.L: Y vino un viajero al hombre rico, y él se privó de tomar de sus ovejas y de sus vacas para preparar[le] al caminante que había venido a él. Y tomó la corderita del hombre pobre y la preparó para el hombre que había venido a él».
es.B: Entonces llegó un viajero a casa del hombre rico. Él no quiso tomar una de sus propias ovejas o reses para preparársela al visitante que había llegado. Así que tomó la corderita del pobre y se la preparó a su huésped».
es.R: Un día llegó un viajero a visitar al hombre rico. El rico no quiso matar ninguna de sus propias ovejas ni de sus reses para hacerle una comida a su invitado. Así que tomó la corderita del hombre pobre y la cocinó para el visitante».

fr.L: Et un voyageur est venu chez l’homme riche, et il a épargné de prendre de son petit bétail et de son gros bétail pour apprêter [un repas] au passant qui était venu chez lui. Et il a pris la brebis de l’homme pauvre et l’a apprêtée pour l’homme qui était venu chez lui. »
fr.B: Un jour, un voyageur est arrivé chez le riche. Celui-ci n’a pas voulu prendre une de ses propres bêtes, mouton ou bœuf, pour la préparer au visiteur venu chez lui. Il a donc pris la brebis du pauvre et l’a préparée pour son hôte. »
fr.R: Un jour, un voyageur est venu rendre visite à l’homme riche. L’homme riche n’a pas voulu tuer un de ses moutons ou un de ses bœufs pour faire un repas à son invité. Alors il a pris l’agnelle de l’homme pauvre et il l’a fait cuire pour le visiteur. »

sw.L: Kisha msafiri akaja kwa yule tajiri, naye akaona uchungu kutwaa katika kundi lake mwenyewe na katika ng'ombe zake mwenyewe ili kumwandalia mpita njia aliyekuja kwake. Akamtwaa mwana-kondoo wa yule maskini akamwandalia mtu aliyekuja kwake."
sw.B: Kisha mgeni alifika kwa yule tajiri. Hakutaka kuchukua mmoja wa kondoo au ng'ombe wake mwenyewe ili kumwandalia mgeni aliyekuja kwake. Basi akamchukua mwana-kondoo wa yule maskini akamwandalia mgeni wake."
sw.R: Siku moja msafiri alikuja kumtembelea yule tajiri. Tajiri hakutaka kumchinja hata mmoja wa kondoo au ng'ombe wake ili kumpikia mgeni wake chakula. Basi akamchukua mwana-kondoo wa yule maskini akampikia mgeni huyo."

vi.L: Có một khách lữ hành đến nhà người giàu, nhưng ông tiếc không lấy chiên hay bò của mình để làm thịt đãi người khách đã đến với mình. Ông bắt con chiên cái của người nghèo và làm thịt nó đãi người khách đã đến với mình."
vi.B: Một hôm có một người khách đi đường ghé nhà người giàu. Ông ta không muốn bắt chiên hay bò của mình làm thịt đãi khách, nên bắt con chiên cái của người nghèo mà làm thịt đãi khách."
vi.R: Một hôm có một người khách đến thăm người giàu. Người giàu không muốn làm thịt chiên hay bò của mình để đãi khách. Vì vậy ông ta bắt con chiên của người nghèo và nấu cho khách ăn."

ko.L: 그런데 나그네 하나가 그 부자에게 왔습니다. 그러나 그는 자기에게 온 길손을 위하여 [음식을] 장만하려고 자기 양 떼와 소 떼에서 가져오기를 아까워했습니다. 그리고 그가 가난한 사람의 암양 새끼를 빼앗아 자기에게 온 사람을 위하여 장만했습니다."
ko.B: 그런데 그 부자에게 나그네가 찾아왔습니다. 부자는 찾아온 손님을 대접하려고 자기 양이나 소를 잡기는 아까웠습니다. 그래서 그는 가난한 사람의 암양 새끼를 빼앗아다가 손님을 위해 요리했습니다."
ko.R: 어느 날 길을 가던 사람이 그 부자를 찾아왔습니다. 부자는 손님에게 대접할 음식을 만들려고 자기 양이나 소를 잡고 싶지 않았습니다. 그래서 그는 가난한 사람의 양을 빼앗아 손님을 위해 요리했습니다."

pt.L: E veio um viajante ao homem rico, e ele teve pena de tomar das suas ovelhas e dos seus bois para preparar [comida] para o viajante que tinha vindo a ele; e tomou a cordeirinha do homem pobre e a preparou para o homem que tinha vindo a ele."
pt.B: Então chegou um viajante à casa do rico. Ele teve pena de tirar uma das suas próprias ovelhas ou um dos seus bois para preparar uma refeição para o visitante que tinha chegado. Por isso tomou a cordeirinha do pobre e a preparou para o seu hóspede."
pt.R: Um dia, um viajante foi visitar o homem rico. O rico não quis matar nenhuma das suas ovelhas nem dos seus bois para fazer uma refeição para o hóspede. Então pegou a cordeirinha do pobre e a cozinhou para o visitante."

decisions.choice: he spared: he was unwilling to part with his own animals
decisions.reason: The verb means to feel pity for something and so hold it back. The rich man "spares" his own animals, yet in verse 6 David condemns him because he "had no pity": the same verb, turned against him.

decisions.choice: a traveler: a guest who had to be fed
decisions.reason: Hospitality was a strict duty, and a guest was given a meal of meat (Genesis 18:1-8). The visitor is named three ways, "a traveler", "the wayfarer" and "the man who had come to him", but he is the same person.

decisions.choice: prepare: kill and cook for a meal
decisions.reason: "To make" or "prepare" an animal for a guest means to slaughter it and cook it (Genesis 18:7-8).

decisions.choice: did not want to (Balanced); visitor, guest (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "did not want to" for "spared", and use "visitor" and "guest" for the three names of the traveler so that it is clear one man is meant.

decisions.choice: One day; kill; make a meal; cooked
decisions.reason: Readable sets the scene with "One day" and spells out what preparing an animal for a guest involved (m3).

decisions.choice: "tiếc" (L); "không muốn" (B, R)
decisions.reason: He was unwilling to part with his own animals (meaning decision); Literal's "tiếc" (begrudge) keeps the link with "had no pity" in verse 6.

decisions.choice: teve pena de tomar (L); teve pena de tirar (B)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "ter pena" covers both sides of the verb: to be sorry to part with something and to feel pity for someone (m1). Literal and Balanced use it here so that David's verdict in verse 6, "não teve pena", turns the same words against the rich man (m4 there). Readable says "não quis", as the English does.

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף דָּוִ֛ד בָּאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־נָתָ֔ן חַי־יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֣י בֶן־מָ֔וֶת הָאִ֖ישׁ הָעֹשֶׂ֥ה זֹֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of David against the man very, and he said to Nathan, [as] lives Yahweh, surely a son of death [is] the man who did this.

en.L: And David's anger burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, the man who did this [is] a son of death!
en.B: David's anger burned hot against the man. "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," he said to Nathan, "the man who did this deserves to die!
en.R: David became very angry with the rich man. "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," he told Nathan, "the man who did this should die!

es.L: Y se encendió mucho la ira de David contra aquel hombre, y dijo a Natán: «¡Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que hijo de muerte [es] el hombre que hizo esto!
es.B: La ira de David se encendió mucho contra aquel hombre. «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive», le dijo a Natán, «¡el hombre que hizo esto merece la muerte!
es.R: David se enojó muchísimo con el hombre rico. «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive», le dijo a Natán, «¡el hombre que hizo esto debe morir!

fr.L: Et la colère de David s’enflamma très fort contre l’homme, et il dit à Nathan : « [Aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, l’homme qui a fait cela [est] un fils de la mort !
fr.B: David s’enflamma de colère contre cet homme. « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, dit-il à Nathan, l’homme qui a fait cela mérite la mort !
fr.R: David s’est mis très en colère contre l’homme riche. « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, a-t-il dit à Nathan, l’homme qui a fait cela devrait mourir !

sw.L: Hasira ya Daudi ikawaka sana juu ya mtu huyo, akamwambia Nathani, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, mtu aliyefanya hivi [ni] mwana wa mauti!
sw.B: Hasira ya Daudi iliwaka sana dhidi ya mtu huyo. Akamwambia Nathani, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, mtu aliyefanya jambo hili anastahili kufa!
sw.R: Daudi alimkasirikia sana yule tajiri. Akamwambia Nathani, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, mtu aliyefanya jambo hili anapaswa kufa!

vi.L: Đa-vít nổi giận phừng phừng với người ấy, và nói với Na-than: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, người đã làm điều này đáng chết!
vi.B: Đa-vít nổi giận phừng phừng với người ấy và nói với Na-than: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, kẻ đã làm điều này đáng phải chết!
vi.R: Đa-vít rất giận người giàu ấy. Vua nói với Na-than: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, kẻ đã làm điều này phải chết!

ko.L: 그러자 다윗이 그 사람에게 몹시 분노하여 나단에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 [두고 맹세하는데], 이 일을 한 사람은 죽어 마땅한 자[이다]!
ko.B: 다윗은 그 사람에게 크게 분노하여 나단에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세하는데, 그런 일을 한 사람은 죽어 마땅하다!
ko.R: 다윗은 그 부자에게 몹시 화가 났다. 그가 나단에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세한다. 그런 짓을 한 사람은 죽어야 한다!

pt.L: E a ira de Davi se acendeu muito contra o homem, e ele disse a Natã: "[Tão certo como] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vive, o homem que fez isso [é] filho da morte!
pt.B: A ira de Davi se acendeu muito contra aquele homem. "Tão certo como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vive", disse ele a Natã, "o homem que fez isso merece morrer!
pt.R: Davi ficou furioso com o homem rico. "Tão certo como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vive", disse ele a Natã, "o homem que fez isso deve morrer!

decisions.choice: as the LORD lives: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: David swears by the life of Yahweh, which binds him to his own verdict (1 Samuel 14:39; 20:3). Without knowing it, he passes sentence on himself under oath.

decisions.choice: a son of death: a man who deserves to die
decisions.reason: "Son of" with a quality means a person marked by it. "Son of death" is someone who deserves death or is doomed to it (1 Samuel 20:31; 26:16).

decisions.choice: a verdict beyond the law
decisions.reason: The law for stealing a sheep was repayment, not death (Exodus 21:37, numbered 22:1 in some Bibles), as David himself goes on to say in verse 6. His outburst shows how wicked the rich man's act seems to him. Some take "son of death" as a cry of contempt ("he deserves to die") rather than a legal sentence.

decisions.choice: deserves to die (Balanced); should die (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m2); Literal keeps "son of death".

decisions.choice: "đáng chết" (L)
decisions.reason: A man who deserves to die (meaning decision); Vietnamese "con của sự chết" would not be understood, so Literal gives the sense in the shortest form.

decisions.choice: "죽어 마땅한 자" at Literal for "a son of death"
decisions.reason: A word-for-word "son of death" would mislead a Korean reader; Literal gives the idiom's sense in a short phrase, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: filho da morte (L); merece morrer (B); deve morrer (R)
decisions.reason: As 1 Samuel 20:31 and 26:16 in Portuguese: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, and Balanced and Readable give its meaning (m2). The oath takes the book's form "tão certo como o SENHOR vive" (m1).

records.literal_gloss: And the ewe-lamb he shall repay fourfold, because that he did the thing the this and because that not he had pity.

en.L: And he shall repay the ewe lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no pity."
en.B: He must pay back four times over for the lamb, because he did this and because he had no pity."
en.R: He must pay the poor man back four lambs for the one he took, because he did this and showed no pity."

es.L: Y la corderita la pagará cuatro veces, por haber hecho esto y por no haber tenido compasión».
es.B: Tendrá que pagar cuatro veces el valor de la corderita, porque hizo esto y no tuvo compasión».
es.R: Tendrá que darle al hombre pobre cuatro corderos por el que le quitó, porque hizo esto y no tuvo compasión».

fr.L: Et la brebis, il la rendra au quadruple, parce qu’il a fait cette chose et parce qu’il n’a pas eu de pitié. »
fr.B: Il devra rendre quatre fois la valeur de la brebis, parce qu’il a fait cela et qu’il n’a pas eu de pitié. »
fr.R: Il devra donner au pauvre quatre agneaux pour celle qu’il a prise, parce qu’il a fait cela et qu’il n’a eu aucune pitié. »

sw.L: Naye atamlipa yule mwana-kondoo mara nne, kwa sababu alifanya jambo hili na kwa sababu hakuona huruma."
sw.B: Lazima alipe mara nne kwa ajili ya yule mwana-kondoo, kwa sababu alifanya jambo hili na kwa sababu hakuwa na huruma."

vi.L: Nó phải đền con chiên cái gấp bốn, vì nó đã làm điều này và vì nó đã không có lòng thương xót."
vi.B: Nó phải đền gấp bốn lần con chiên ấy, vì nó đã làm điều này và không có lòng thương xót."
vi.R: Nó phải đền cho người nghèo bốn con chiên thay cho con nó đã bắt, vì nó đã làm điều này và không biết thương xót."

ko.L: 그리고 그가 그 암양 새끼를 네 배로 갚아야 한다. 그가 이런 일을 했고 불쌍히 여기지 않았기 때문이다."
ko.B: 그는 그 양 한 마리를 네 배로 갚아야 한다. 그가 이런 일을 저질렀고, 조금도 불쌍히 여기지 않았기 때문이다."
ko.R: 그는 가난한 사람에게 빼앗은 양 한 마리 대신에 네 마리를 갚아 주어야 한다. 그가 그런 짓을 했고 남을 불쌍히 여기지 않았기 때문이다."

pt.L: E ele restituirá a cordeirinha quatro vezes, porque fez esta coisa e porque não teve pena."
pt.B: Ele terá de pagar quatro vezes o valor da cordeirinha, porque fez isso e porque não teve pena."
pt.R: Ele terá de dar ao pobre quatro cordeiros no lugar da cordeirinha que tomou, porque fez isso e não teve pena dele."

decisions.choice: repay fourfold: the penalty the law set for a stolen sheep
decisions.reason: Exodus 21:37 (numbered 22:1 in some Bibles) says that whoever steals a sheep and slaughters it must repay four sheep for it. David the judge applies the law exactly.

decisions.choice: fourfold, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation read "sevenfold", a number used for full repayment in Proverbs 6:31. The Hebrew reading agrees with the law of Exodus 21:37 and is followed.

decisions.choice: fourfold: a number that may look ahead in David's story
decisions.reason: Readers have long noticed that four of David's sons die in what follows: the child (verse 18), Amnon (13:28-29), Absalom (18:14-15) and Adonijah (1 Kings 2:25). The text does not draw this link itself.

decisions.choice: he had no pity: the same verb as "spared" in verse 4
decisions.reason: The rich man was sparing with his own flock but had no pity on the poor man. The wordplay sharpens the charge.

decisions.choice: pay the poor man back four lambs for the one he took
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "fourfold" means here.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר נָתָ֛ן אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד אַתָּ֣ה הָאִ֑ישׁ כֹּה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָנֹכִ֞י מְשַׁחְתִּ֤יךָֽ לְמֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָנֹכִ֥י הִצַּלְתִּ֖יךָ מִיַּ֥ד שָׁאֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Nathan to David, you [are] the man! Thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, I anointed you as king over Israel, and I delivered you from [the] hand of Saul.

en.L: And Nathan said to David, "You [are] the man! Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: 'I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.
en.B: Nathan said to David, "You are the man! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: 'I anointed you king over Israel, and I rescued you from Saul's power.
en.R: Then Nathan said to David, "You are that man! And this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: 'I am the one who anointed you to be king over Israel, and I rescued you from Saul.

es.L: Y dijo Natán a David: «¡Tú [eres] el hombre! Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: “Yo te ungí como rey sobre Israel, y yo te libré de la mano de Saúl.
es.B: Natán le dijo a David: «¡Tú eres ese hombre! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: “Yo te ungí rey sobre Israel, y yo te libré del poder de Saúl.
es.R: Entonces Natán le dijo a David: «¡Ese hombre eres tú! Y esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: “Yo soy quien te ungió como rey de Israel, y yo te salvé de Saúl.

fr.L: Et Nathan dit à David : « Toi, [tu es] l’homme ! Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël : “C’est moi qui t’ai oint comme roi sur Israël, et c’est moi qui t’ai délivré de la main de Saül.
fr.B: Nathan dit à David : « Cet homme, c’est toi ! {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : “Je t’ai oint comme roi sur Israël, et je t’ai délivré du pouvoir de Saül.
fr.R: Alors Nathan a dit à David : « Cet homme, c’est toi ! Et voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël : “C’est moi qui t’ai oint pour que tu sois roi sur Israël, et c’est moi qui t’ai délivré de Saül.

sw.L: Nathani akamwambia Daudi, "Mtu huyo [ni] wewe! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: 'Mimi nilikupaka mafuta uwe mfalme juu ya Israeli, nami nilikuokoa kutoka mkononi mwa Sauli.
sw.B: Nathani akamwambia Daudi, "Mtu huyo ni wewe! Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: 'Nilikupaka mafuta uwe mfalme juu ya Israeli, nami nikakuokoa kutoka katika nguvu za Sauli.
sw.R: Kisha Nathani akamwambia Daudi, "Mtu huyo ni wewe! Na hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: 'Mimi ndiye niliyekupaka mafuta uwe mfalme juu ya Israeli, nami nikakuokoa kutoka kwa Sauli.

vi.L: Na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Chính vua là người đó! {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên phán thế này: 'Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã xức dầu cho ngươi làm vua trên Y-sơ-ra-ên, và chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giải cứu ngươi khỏi tay Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Chính vua là người đó! {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán như vầy: 'Ta đã xức dầu cho ngươi làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giải cứu ngươi khỏi quyền lực của Sau-lơ.
vi.R: Bấy giờ Na-than nói với Đa-vít: "Vua chính là người đó! Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán: 'Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã xức dầu cho ngươi làm vua Y-sơ-ra-ên, và chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã giải cứu ngươi khỏi tay Sau-lơ.

ko.L: 그러자 나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "임금님이 그 사람[입니다]! 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하십니다. '내가 너에게 기름을 부어 이스라엘의 왕으로 세웠고, 내가 너를 사울의 손에서 건져 내었다.
ko.B: 나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "임금님이 바로 그 사람입니다! 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하십니다. '내가 너에게 기름을 부어 이스라엘의 왕으로 세웠고, 사울의 손에서 너를 건져 주었다.
ko.R: 그때 나단이 다윗에게 말했다. "임금님이 바로 그 사람입니다! 이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀을 들으십시오. '너에게 기름을 부어 이스라엘의 왕으로 세운 것은 바로 나다. 너를 사울에게서 구해 준 것도 나다.

pt.L: E Natã disse a Davi: "Você [é] o homem! Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: 'Eu te ungi rei sobre Israel, e eu te livrei da mão de Saul.
pt.B: Natã disse a Davi: "Esse homem é você! Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: 'Eu te ungi rei sobre Israel e te livrei do poder de Saul.
pt.R: Então Natã disse a Davi: "Esse homem é você! E é isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, diz: 'Fui eu que te ungi como rei de Israel, e fui eu que te livrei de Saul.

decisions.choice: You are the man: the verdict turns on the judge
decisions.reason: In Hebrew these are two short words, "you the man". David has just condemned "the man who did this" (verse 5); Nathan's reply applies that verdict to him.

decisions.choice: I ... I: God stresses that he himself acted
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun "I" before each verb, which it does not need. The emphasis falls on what God, not David, had done: everything David has, he received.

decisions.choice: I anointed you ... I delivered you: the story of 1 Samuel
decisions.reason: Samuel anointed David at God's command (1 Samuel 16:12-13), and God kept him safe through the years when Saul hunted him (1 Samuel 19-26).

decisions.choice: rescued you from Saul's power (Balanced); rescued you from Saul (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power; Balanced says "power" and Readable leaves the picture out. Readable shows the emphatic "I" of m2 with "I am the one who".

decisions.choice: single quotes for God's words inside Nathan's speech
decisions.reason: The words Nathan reports from God are set in single quotes inside his own speech. They run to the end of verse 10; verse 11 opens a second saying of God, which runs to the end of verse 12.

decisions.choice: Toi, [tu es] l'homme ! (L); Cet homme, c'est toi ! (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is two words, "you the man" (m1). Literal keeps that order; Balanced and Readable put "cet homme" first and end on "toi", so the verdict falls on David as the sentence closes. God's words inside Nathan's speech take “ ” within « ».

decisions.choice: God's words in “ ” inside Nathan's «»
decisions.reason: As set at 1:3 for Spanish: the words Nathan reports from God are a quotation inside his speech, so they take the inner quotes “ ”, as the English takes single quotes.

decisions.choice: Nathan speaks to the king in 합쇼체; God's words inside his speech are in 해라체 with "너", set in single quotation marks
alternatives: God's words reported in the polite style
decisions.reason: As the Korean style guide: God speaks 해라체, and the prophet passes on God's own words as spoken. The messenger formula takes the honorific ("말씀하십니다") because Nathan is speaking to the king.

decisions.choice: "Chính vua là người đó!"
decisions.reason: The verdict turns on the judge (meaning decision); Nathan keeps calling David "vua", and "chính" carries the Hebrew's sharp "you".

decisions.choice: God calls David "ngươi" at every level in this judgment
decisions.reason: God's words to a king he is judging keep "ngươi" at every level (5:2); the distance marks the judgment after the promise of chapter 7. Nathan himself calls David "vua".

decisions.choice: Você [é] o homem! (L); Esse homem é você! (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "você" last, where Portuguese puts the stress: the verdict David has just given on "the man who did this" (verse 5) lands on him (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew order and brackets the verb.

decisions.choice: Natã: você; God's words: tu ("te ungi", "te livrei")
decisions.reason: Nathan speaks to the king with "você", with the authority of a prophet, as Samuel does to Saul in 1 Samuel (13:11); the words he reports from God say "tu", as God speaks to David throughout. David's own words to Nathan in this chapter (verses 5 and 13) have no second person; where he addresses the prophet in this book he says "você".

source.text: וָאֶתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית אֲדֹנֶ֗יךָ וְאֶת־נְשֵׁ֤י אֲדֹנֶ֨יךָ֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לְךָ֔ אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וְאִ֨ם־מְעָ֔ט וְאֹסִ֥פָה לְּךָ֖ כָּהֵ֥נָּה וְכָהֵֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I gave to you [the] house of your master and [the] wives of your master into your bosom, and I gave to you [the] house of Israel and Judah; and if [that were] too little, then I would add to you like these and like these.

en.L: And I gave you your master's house, and your master's wives into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if [that were] too little, I would have added to you as much again and as much again.
en.B: I gave you your master's house and placed your master's wives in your embrace. I gave you the house of Israel and Judah too. And had that been too little, I would have given you much more besides.
en.R: I gave you all that had belonged to your master Saul, and I put his wives into your arms. I gave you the people of Israel and Judah to rule. If that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.

es.L: Y te di la casa de tu señor, y las mujeres de tu señor en tu regazo, y te di la casa de Israel y de Judá. Y si [eso fuera] poco, te habría añadido otro tanto y otro tanto.
es.B: Te di la casa de tu señor y puse en tus brazos a las mujeres de tu señor. También te di la casa de Israel y de Judá. Y si eso hubiera sido poco, te habría dado mucho más.
es.R: Te di todo lo que había sido de tu señor Saúl, y puse a sus mujeres en tus brazos. Te di al pueblo de Israel y de Judá para que lo gobernaras. Si eso no hubiera sido suficiente, te habría dado mucho más.

fr.L: Et je t’ai donné la maison de ton maître, et les femmes de ton maître dans ton sein, et je t’ai donné la maison d’Israël et de Juda. Et si [c’était] trop peu, je t’y aurais ajouté autant et encore autant.
fr.B: Je t’ai donné la maison de ton maître et j’ai mis dans tes bras les femmes de ton maître. Je t’ai donné aussi la maison d’Israël et de Juda. Et si cela n’avait pas suffi, je t’aurais donné bien davantage encore.
fr.R: Je t’ai donné tout ce qui appartenait à ton maître Saül, et j’ai mis ses femmes dans tes bras. Je t’ai donné le peuple d’Israël et de Juda pour que tu le gouvernes. Si cela n’avait pas suffi, je t’aurais donné encore beaucoup plus.

sw.L: Nilikupa nyumba ya bwana wako, na wake za bwana wako kifuani mwako, nami nikakupa nyumba ya Israeli na Yuda. Na kama [hayo yangekuwa] machache, ningekuongezea mengi kama hayo na mengi kama hayo.
sw.B: Nilikupa nyumba ya bwana wako, nikawaweka wake za bwana wako mikononi mwako. Nikakupa pia nyumba ya Israeli na Yuda. Na kama hayo yangekuwa machache, ningekupa mengi zaidi.
sw.R: Nilikupa vyote vilivyokuwa vya bwana wako Sauli, nikawaweka wake zake mikononi mwako. Nilikupa watu wa Israeli na Yuda uwatawale. Kama hayo yasingetosha, ningekupa mengi zaidi.

vi.L: Ta đã ban cho ngươi nhà của chủ ngươi, và các vợ của chủ ngươi vào lòng ngươi, và đã ban cho ngươi nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa. Nếu [điều đó] còn quá ít, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} còn thêm cho ngươi bằng ấy và bằng ấy nữa.
vi.B: Ta đã ban cho ngươi nhà của chủ ngươi và đặt các vợ của chủ ngươi vào vòng tay ngươi. Ta cũng đã ban cho ngươi nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa. Nếu bấy nhiêu còn quá ít, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ còn ban thêm cho ngươi nhiều hơn nữa.
vi.R: Ta đã ban cho ngươi mọi thứ trước kia thuộc về Sau-lơ, chủ ngươi, và đặt các vợ của người vào vòng tay ngươi. Ta đã ban cho ngươi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa để cai trị. Nếu bấy nhiêu chưa đủ, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ còn ban cho ngươi nhiều hơn nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 너에게 네 주인의 집을 주었고, 네 주인의 아내들을 네 품에 [안겨] 주었으며, 이스라엘과 유다의 집을 너에게 주었다. 그리고 만일 [그것이] 적었다면, 내가 너에게 이것저것을 더 주었을 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 네 주인의 집안을 너에게 주었고, 네 주인의 아내들을 네 품에 안겨 주었다. 이스라엘과 유다 집안도 너에게 주었다. 그것으로 부족했다면, 나는 너에게 얼마든지 더 주었을 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 네 주인 사울이 가졌던 모든 것을 너에게 주었고, 그의 아내들을 네 품에 안겨 주었다. 이스라엘과 유다 백성을 다스리게 해 주었다. 그것으로 모자랐다면, 나는 너에게 훨씬 더 많이 주었을 것이다.

pt.L: E eu te dei a casa do teu senhor, e as mulheres do teu senhor no teu colo, e te dei a casa de Israel e de Judá; e, se [isso fosse] pouco, eu te acrescentaria outro tanto e mais outro tanto.
pt.B: Eu te dei a casa do teu senhor e pus as mulheres do teu senhor nos teus braços. Também te dei a casa de Israel e de Judá. E, se isso tivesse sido pouco, eu te teria dado ainda muito mais.
pt.R: Eu te dei tudo o que tinha pertencido ao teu senhor Saul, e pus as mulheres dele nos teus braços. Eu te dei o povo de Israel e de Judá para governar. Se isso não fosse suficiente, eu te teria dado muito mais.

decisions.choice: your master's house: Saul's household and property
decisions.reason: "House" here is Saul's royal household, with its property and lands (9:7-9). "The house of Israel and Judah" then names the two parts of the people David now rules (2:4; 5:1-5).

decisions.choice: your master's wives into your bosom: Saul's royal household passed to David
decisions.reason: A new king took over the household of the old one, and taking a king's wives was a claim to his throne (16:21-22; 1 Kings 2:22). The books do not record that David married any of Saul's wives; the words may mean that all of Saul's household was placed under David's authority. The phrase also prepares for the charge of verse 9: David, who was given so much, took the one wife of another man.

decisions.choice: like these and like these: as much again, and more
decisions.reason: The doubled phrase means "so much and so much more". God would have given David still more if he had asked.

decisions.choice: your master Saul; the people of Israel and Judah to rule
decisions.reason: Readable names Saul and explains "the house of Israel and Judah" as the people David was given to rule.

decisions.choice: no teu colo (L); nos teus braços (B)
decisions.reason: The word is the "bosom" of the lamb in verse 3, so each level uses the word it used there, "colo" at Literal and "braços" at Balanced, and the reader can hear the link the story makes.

records.literal_gloss: Why have you despised [the] word of Yahweh to do the evil in my eyes? Uriah the Hittite you struck down with the sword, and his wife you took for yourself as a wife, and him you killed with [the] sword of [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: Why have you despised the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, doing what [is] evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes? Uriah the Hittite you struck down with the sword, and his wife you took to be your wife, and him you killed with the sword of the sons of Ammon.
en.B: Why have you despised the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by doing what is evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight? You struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword and took his wife to be your wife. You killed him with the sword of the Ammonites.
en.R: Why have you treated the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with contempt? Why have you done what is evil in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes? You struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword and took his wife as your own. You used the swords of the Ammonites to kill him.

es.L: ¿Por qué has despreciado la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, haciendo lo malo a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos? A Urías el hitita heriste a espada, y a su mujer tomaste para que fuera tu mujer, y a él lo mataste con la espada de los hijos de Amón.
es.B: ¿Por qué has despreciado la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} haciendo lo que es malo ante {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos? Heriste a espada a Urías el hitita y tomaste a su mujer para hacerla tu esposa. Lo mataste con la espada de los amonitas.
es.R: ¿Por qué has tratado con desprecio la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? ¿Por qué has hecho lo que es malo a {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos? Heriste a espada a Urías el hitita y te quedaste con su esposa. Usaste las espadas de los amonitas para matarlo.

fr.L: Pourquoi as-tu méprisé la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, en faisant ce qui [est] mal à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux ? Urie le Hittite, tu l’as frappé par l’épée, et sa femme, tu l’as prise pour en faire ta femme, et lui, tu l’as tué par l’épée des fils d’Ammon.
fr.B: Pourquoi as-tu méprisé la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} en faisant ce qui est mal à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux ? Tu as frappé par l’épée Urie le Hittite et tu as pris sa femme pour en faire ta femme. Tu l’as tué par l’épée des Ammonites.
fr.R: Pourquoi as-tu traité avec mépris la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Pourquoi as-tu fait ce qui est mal à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux ? Tu as frappé Urie le Hittite avec l’épée et tu as pris sa femme pour toi. Tu t’es servi des épées des Ammonites pour le tuer.

sw.L: Kwa nini umelidharau neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ukifanya [yaliyo] mabaya machoni {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}? Uria Mhiti umempiga kwa upanga, na mke wake umemtwaa kuwa mke wako, naye umemwua kwa upanga wa wana wa Amoni.
sw.B: Kwa nini umelidharau neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa kufanya yaliyo mabaya machoni {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}? Umempiga Uria Mhiti kwa upanga, ukamtwaa mke wake awe mke wako. Umemwua kwa upanga wa Waamoni.
sw.R: Kwa nini umelidharau neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}? Kwa nini umefanya yaliyo mabaya machoni {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}? Umempiga Uria Mhiti kwa upanga ukamchukua mke wake kuwa wako. Uliitumia mipanga ya Waamoni kumwua.

vi.L: Sao ngươi đã khinh dể lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, làm điều ác trong mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? U-ri người Hê-tít, ngươi đã dùng gươm đánh giết; vợ người, ngươi đã lấy làm vợ mình; còn người, ngươi đã giết bằng gươm của con cháu Am-môn.
vi.B: Sao ngươi lại khinh dể lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà làm điều ác trước mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? Ngươi đã dùng gươm giết U-ri người Hê-tít và lấy vợ người làm vợ mình. Ngươi đã giết người bằng gươm của người Am-môn.
vi.R: Sao ngươi lại coi thường lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}? Sao ngươi lại làm điều ác trước mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? Ngươi đã dùng gươm giết U-ri người Hê-tít và lấy vợ người làm vợ mình. Ngươi đã dùng gươm của người Am-môn để giết người.

ko.L: 어찌하여 너는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀을 업신여겨 내 눈에 악한 것을 행했느냐? 헷 사람 우리야를 너는 칼로 쳤고, 그의 아내를 너는 네 아내로 삼았으며, 그를 너는 암몬 자손의 칼로 죽였다.
ko.B: 어찌하여 너는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀을 업신여기고, 내가 보기에 악한 짓을 저질렀느냐? 너는 헷 사람 우리야를 칼로 쳐 죽이고 그의 아내를 빼앗아 네 아내로 삼았다. 너는 암몬 사람들의 칼을 빌려 그를 죽였다.
ko.R: 어찌하여 너는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 말씀을 하찮게 여겼느냐? 어찌하여 내가 보기에 악한 일을 했느냐? 너는 헷 사람 우리야를 칼로 쳐 죽이고 그의 아내를 네 아내로 삼았다. 너는 암몬 사람들의 칼을 써서 그를 죽였다.

pt.L: Por que desprezaste a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, fazendo o que [é] mau aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos? Urias, o hitita, feriste à espada, e a mulher dele tomaste para ti como mulher, e a ele mataste com a espada dos filhos de Amom.
pt.B: Por que desprezaste a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, fazendo o que é mau aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos? Feriste à espada Urias, o hitita, e tomaste a mulher dele para ser tua mulher. Tu o mataste com a espada dos amonitas.
pt.R: Por que trataste com desprezo a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}? Por que fizeste o que é mau aos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} olhos? Feriste Urias, o hitita, com a espada e tomaste a mulher dele para ti. Usaste as espadas dos amonitas para matá-lo.

decisions.choice: in my eyes, the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "in his eyes", meaning in Yahweh's eyes; the scribes marked "in my eyes" to be read aloud (qere), which fits God speaking. The sense is the same. It also answers 11:25, where David told Joab not to let the matter be "evil in your eyes", and 11:27, where it was evil in Yahweh's eyes.

decisions.choice: despised the word of the LORD: treated God's commands as worthless
decisions.reason: To "despise" is to treat something with contempt. The "word" here is what Yahweh had commanded, including "You shall not murder" and "You shall not commit adultery" (Exodus 20:13-14). In verse 10 the charge becomes sharper: David despised God himself.

decisions.choice: Uriah ... his wife ... him: each placed first for emphasis
decisions.reason: Each charge begins with its object, which the Hebrew word order sets first for weight: Uriah, his wife, and Uriah again. David used the enemy's sword to kill him (11:14-17).

decisions.choice: You struck down Uriah ... took his wife ... You killed him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the objects in the usual English order; Literal keeps the Hebrew order (m3).

decisions.choice: treated ... with contempt; two questions
decisions.reason: Readable explains "despised" and splits the long question in two.

decisions.choice: "A Urías el hitita heriste ... a su mujer tomaste ... a él lo mataste" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, with each object placed first for emphasis; Spanish can do this naturally with the personal "a" and a resumptive "lo".

decisions.choice: Literal keeps the Hebrew's emphasis by putting "헷 사람 우리야를", "그의 아내를" and "그를" first, each followed by "너는"
alternatives: the ordinary order at Literal too
decisions.reason: Korean allows the object first with the subject after it, which carries the stress the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "U-ri người Hê-tít, ngươi đã ... vợ người, ngươi đã ... còn người, ngươi đã ..." (L)
decisions.reason: Each object is placed first for emphasis (meaning decision); Vietnamese can front them with a comma, so Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

decisions.choice: mau aos meus olhos (every level)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "mau aos ... olhos", the words of 11:25 and 11:27 in Portuguese (m1), so that the chain can be followed from David's message to Joab to God's charge.

records.literal_gloss: And now not shall depart [the] sword from your house until forever, because you despised me and took [the] wife of Uriah the Hittite to be for you as a wife.

en.B: So now the sword will never depart from your house, because you despised {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.'
en.R: So now violence and killing will never leave your family, because you treated {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with contempt. You took the wife of Uriah the Hittite and made her your own.'

es.L: Y ahora no se apartará jamás la espada de tu casa, porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} despreciaste y tomaste la mujer de Urías el hitita para que fuera tu mujer”.

es.R: Por eso, ahora la violencia y la muerte nunca se apartarán de tu familia, porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} trataste con desprecio. Tomaste a la esposa de Urías el hitita y la hiciste tuya”.

fr.L: Et maintenant, l’épée ne s’écartera jamais de ta maison, parce que tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as méprisé et que tu as pris la femme d’Urie le Hittite pour qu’elle soit ta femme.”
fr.B: Désormais, l’épée ne s’éloignera jamais de ta maison, parce que tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as méprisé et que tu as pris la femme d’Urie le Hittite pour en faire ta femme.”
fr.R: Alors maintenant, la violence et le meurtre ne quitteront jamais ta famille, parce que tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as traité avec mépris. Tu as pris la femme d’Urie le Hittite et tu en as fait ta femme.”

sw.R: Kwa hiyo sasa mauaji na mapigano hayataiacha kamwe jamaa yako, kwa sababu umenidharau {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Ulimchukua mke wa Uria Mhiti ukamfanya kuwa wako.'

vi.R: Vậy bây giờ, bạo lực và chết chóc sẽ không bao giờ rời khỏi gia đình ngươi, vì ngươi đã coi thường {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ngươi đã lấy vợ của U-ri người Hê-tít làm vợ mình.'

ko.B: 그러므로 이제 칼이 네 집안에서 영원히 떠나지 않을 것이다. 네가 나를 업신여기고 헷 사람 우리야의 아내를 빼앗아 네 아내로 삼았기 때문이다.'
ko.R: 그러므로 이제 폭력과 죽음이 네 집안에서 영원히 떠나지 않을 것이다. 네가 나를 하찮게 여겼기 때문이다. 너는 헷 사람 우리야의 아내를 빼앗아 네 아내로 삼았다.'

pt.L: E agora a espada não se afastará da tua casa para sempre, porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} desprezaste e tomaste a mulher de Urias, o hitita, para ser tua mulher.'
pt.B: Por isso, agora, a espada nunca se afastará da tua casa, porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} desprezaste e tomaste a mulher de Urias, o hitita, para ser tua mulher.'
pt.R: Por isso, agora a violência e as mortes nunca vão sair da tua família, porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} trataste com desprezo. Tomaste a mulher de Urias, o hitita, e fizeste dela tua mulher.'

decisions.choice: the sword shall not depart from your house: violent death will stay in David's family
decisions.reason: As David killed Uriah by the sword, so the sword will strike his own house. The story goes on to show it: Amnon is murdered by Absalom (13:28-29), Absalom dies in battle against his father (18:14-15), and Adonijah is put to death (1 Kings 2:25).

decisions.choice: forever: for the generations to come
decisions.reason: The phrase means a long and lasting time, here the life of David's dynasty, not without end. It answers the promise of 7:13-16, that God's faithful love would not depart from David's house: that promise stands, but so does this judgment.

decisions.choice: you despised me: to despise God's word is to despise God
decisions.reason: Verse 9 said David despised Yahweh's word; here God says David despised him. The sin was not only against Uriah but against God himself (verse 13).

decisions.choice: violence and killing; your family
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the sword" and says "family" for "house".

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, behold, I [am] raising against you evil from your house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give [them] to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives in [the] eyes of the sun the this.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Look, I am raising up evil against you out of your own house. And I will take your wives before your eyes and give [them] to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'I am about to raise up disaster against you from within your own household. Before your eyes I will take your wives and give them to one who is close to you, and he will lie with your wives in broad daylight.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'I am going to bring trouble on you from your own family. While you watch, I will take your wives and give them to another man, and he will sleep with them in the light of day.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “He aquí, yo levanto contra ti el mal de tu propia casa. Y tomaré a tus mujeres delante de tus ojos y [las] daré a tu prójimo, y él se acostará con tus mujeres a la vista de este sol.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: “Voy a hacer que la desgracia se levante contra ti desde tu propia casa. Delante de tus ojos tomaré a tus mujeres y se las daré a uno que está cerca de ti, y él se acostará con tus mujeres a plena luz del día.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: “Voy a traer desgracia sobre ti desde tu propia familia. Mientras tú lo ves, tomaré a tus mujeres y se las daré a otro hombre, y él se acostará con ellas a la luz del día.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : “Voici, je fais surgir contre toi le malheur de ta propre maison. Et je prendrai tes femmes sous tes yeux et je [les] donnerai à ton prochain, et il couchera avec tes femmes aux yeux de ce soleil.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : “Je vais faire venir sur toi le malheur du sein même de ta maison. Sous tes yeux, je prendrai tes femmes et je les donnerai à un de tes proches, et il couchera avec elles en plein jour.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : “Je vais faire venir le malheur sur toi à partir de ta propre famille. Pendant que tu regarderas, je prendrai tes femmes et je les donnerai à un autre homme, et il couchera avec elles à la lumière du jour.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: 'Tazama, mimi ninakuinulia mabaya kutoka katika nyumba yako mwenyewe. Nami nitawatwaa wake zako mbele ya macho yako na kumpa jirani yako, naye atalala na wake zako machoni pa jua hili.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: 'Nitakuletea maafa kutoka ndani ya nyumba yako mwenyewe. Mbele ya macho yako nitawachukua wake zako na kumpa mtu aliye karibu nawe, naye atalala na wake zako mchana kweupe.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: 'Nitakuletea taabu kutoka katika jamaa yako mwenyewe. Ukiwa unatazama, nitawachukua wake zako na kumpa mwanamume mwingine, naye atalala nao waziwazi mchana.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: 'Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ dấy tai họa lên nghịch cùng ngươi từ chính nhà ngươi. Ta sẽ bắt các vợ ngươi trước mắt ngươi mà trao cho kẻ lân cận ngươi, và nó sẽ nằm với các vợ ngươi trước mặt mặt trời này.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: 'Ta sắp dấy tai họa lên nghịch cùng ngươi từ chính trong nhà ngươi. Ngay trước mắt ngươi, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ bắt các vợ ngươi mà trao cho một người thân cận với ngươi, và người ấy sẽ ăn nằm với các vợ ngươi giữa ban ngày.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: 'Ta sẽ khiến tai họa đến trên ngươi từ chính gia đình ngươi. Ngay trước mắt ngươi, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ bắt các vợ ngươi mà trao cho một người đàn ông khác, và người ấy sẽ ngủ với họ giữa thanh thiên bạch nhật.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하십니다. '보아라, 내가 네 집에서 너를 칠 재앙을 일으키겠다. 그리고 내가 네 눈앞에서 네 아내들을 빼앗아 네 이웃에게 줄 것이니, 그가 이 해가 보는 앞에서 네 아내들과 함께 누울 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하십니다. '내가 네 집안에서 재앙을 일으켜 너를 치겠다. 네가 보는 앞에서 네 아내들을 빼앗아 너와 가까운 사람에게 주겠다. 그가 대낮에 네 아내들과 잠자리를 같이할 것이다.
ko.R: 이것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀입니다. '내가 네 집안사람을 통해 너에게 재앙을 내리겠다. 네가 보는 앞에서 네 아내들을 빼앗아 다른 남자에게 주겠다. 그가 환한 대낮에 네 아내들과 함께 잘 것이다.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: 'Eis que estou levantando contra ti o mal da tua própria casa. E tomarei as tuas mulheres diante dos teus olhos e [as] darei ao teu próximo, e ele se deitará com as tuas mulheres aos olhos deste sol.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: 'Vou fazer surgir contra ti a desgraça de dentro da tua própria família. Diante dos teus olhos tomarei as tuas mulheres e as darei a alguém próximo de ti, e ele se deitará com as tuas mulheres em plena luz do dia.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: 'Vou trazer desgraça sobre ti, e ela virá da tua própria família. Diante dos teus olhos, tomarei as tuas mulheres e as darei a outro homem, e ele dormirá com elas à luz do dia.

decisions.choice: evil: harm, disaster
decisions.reason: The word can mean moral evil or harm that comes on someone. Here it is the harm God will bring, an answer to the evil David did (verse 9).

decisions.choice: your neighbor: another man, one close to you
decisions.reason: The word means a fellow or companion, anyone besides oneself (1 Samuel 15:28). The words "from your own house" show that it will be someone from David's own family.

decisions.choice: he will lie with your wives: fulfilled through Absalom
decisions.reason: When Absalom rebels, he lies with his father's concubines in a tent on the roof of the palace, in the sight of all Israel (16:21-22).

decisions.choice: in the eyes of this sun: openly, in broad daylight
decisions.reason: The sun is pictured as a witness that sees everything. What David did in secret (verse 12) will be paid back in the open.

decisions.choice: in broad daylight (Balanced); in the light of day (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m4).

decisions.choice: another man; sleep with them
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "your neighbor" and "lie with".

decisions.choice: "trước mặt mặt trời này" (L); "giữa ban ngày" (B); "giữa thanh thiên bạch nhật" (R)
decisions.reason: Openly, in broad daylight (meaning decision); Literal keeps the sun, Readable uses the Vietnamese idiom for "in full daylight", which every reader knows.

decisions.choice: you ... I: two emphatic pronouns set side by side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew places "you" and "I" in contrast: David hid his deed, but God will act in public.

decisions.choice: before the sun: openly
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the sun stands for full daylight and public view.

decisions.choice: sinned; openly
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what David did in secret and adds "openly" to make the contrast clear.

decisions.choice: both quotations close
decisions.reason: God's second saying (single quotes) and Nathan's speech (double quotes) both end here.

decisions.choice: I have sinned against the LORD: a confession without excuse
decisions.reason: David makes no defense. He names his sin as sin against Yahweh himself, though Uriah and Bathsheba were the ones wronged (compare Psalm 51:6). The title of Psalm 51 (Hebrew 51:1-2) links that psalm to this moment.

decisions.choice: has put away your sin: has removed it, forgiven it
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something pass over or pass away. Yahweh takes the guilt away from David (24:10; Job 7:21).

decisions.choice: also: on his part
decisions.reason: The small word "also" answers David's confession: David has confessed, and Yahweh for his part has removed the sin. It can also simply add weight ("indeed").

decisions.choice: you will not die: the death David deserved is not carried out
decisions.reason: Under the law adultery and murder were both punished by death (Leviticus 20:10; Numbers 35:31). David had also spoken the sentence "son of death" over the man in the story (verse 5).

decisions.choice: has taken away (Balanced and Readable, without "also")
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out "also", whose force English carries by the order of the two speeches (m3); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: Nathan's speech continues into verse 14
decisions.reason: Nathan's answer runs on into the next verse, so its quotation closes there.

decisions.choice: David says "tôi", not the king's "ta", in his confession
decisions.reason: Confessing his sin before God's prophet, David does not speak as king; the plain "tôi" keeps the confession without excuse (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Pequei contra o SENHOR (every level)
decisions.reason: David's confession is two words in Hebrew (m1), and Portuguese keeps it as short at every level: "Pequei" needs no pronoun, and the same words serve all three levels.

decisions.choice: the enemies of the LORD, as the Hebrew text reads
alternatives: you have utterly scorned the LORD (the probable earlier wording)
decisions.reason: The words "the enemies of" were probably added by scribes so that the text would not say outright that David scorned Yahweh. Scribes softened other places where a curse or insult would fall on God or his chosen king in the same way (compare 1 Samuel 25:22, "the enemies of David"). Without the added words the sentence reads "you have utterly scorned Yahweh". The Hebrew text is followed, but its sense is that David's deed was contempt for Yahweh himself, as verses 9-10 have said.

decisions.choice: you have utterly given cause to scorn
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. With "the enemies of Yahweh" as its object, it is read here as "made them scorn": David's deed has given God's enemies reason to despise him. Elsewhere the same form means simply "scorn" (Isaiah 1:4), and that is its sense if the words "the enemies of" are a later softening (m1).

decisions.choice: the son will die: forgiveness does not undo every consequence
decisions.reason: David himself will not die (verse 13), but the child born from his adultery will. The judgment of the sword on his house (verse 10) also still stands.

decisions.choice: nevertheless, because: a turn after forgiveness
decisions.reason: The opening word limits what was just said: the sin is put away, but something remains.

decisions.choice: every reason to scorn him (Balanced); to look down on him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "him", the one scorned, which the reading of m2 implies; Literal leaves it unexpressed.

decisions.choice: two sentences joined by "So"
decisions.reason: Readable splits the verse and states the cause first.

decisions.choice: the wife of Uriah: the narrator still names her by her husband
decisions.reason: The child's mother is called "the wife of Uriah", not "David's wife", keeping the wrong in view. Only after the child's death, in verse 24, is she named Bathsheba, David's wife.

decisions.choice: became very sick: fell seriously, hopelessly ill
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a wound or sickness that cannot be cured (Jeremiah 17:9; Micah 1:9; Job 34:6).

decisions.choice: the LORD struck the child
decisions.reason: The illness is presented as God's act, carrying out the word of verse 14.

decisions.choice: he (not "it") for the child
decisions.reason: The child is the son of verse 14, so a personal pronoun is used. Readable repeats "the baby" for clarity.

decisions.choice: "đứa trẻ", "đứa bé", "nó" for the child
decisions.reason: Vietnamese speaks of a baby with "đứa bé" and "nó", which are tender, not dismissive; the English "he" rather than "it" has no counterpart to lose.

decisions.choice: o menino (L, B); o bebê (R)
decisions.reason: The child is the son of verse 14, so Literal and Balanced say "o menino", which lets "ele" follow as in the English; "a criança" is feminine in Portuguese and would make the pronouns "ela". Readable says "o bebê", as the English says "the baby".
